definition: Improvised means made up or put together on the spot, from whatever is at hand, without preparation.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word improvised. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know improvised should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: With the bridge out, the crew rigged an improvised ferry from two barges and a tow cable.
Unrehearsed is milder than improvised: an unrehearsed speech may still follow careful notes, while an improvised one is invented on the spot with nothing prepared at all.
Slapdash goes further than improvised: an improvised repair is unplanned but resourceful, while a slapdash one is thrown together with so little care that it cannot be trusted.

Impromptu means done without preparation, but it belongs to the things people say and perform — toasts, speeches, recitals. Improvised covers made things too: a shelter, a splint, a signal can all be improvised.

Spontaneous describes why something happened — a sudden inner impulse, with nobody planning it. Improvised describes how: pieced together in the moment from whatever was at hand, whether the reason was impulse or necessity.

Makeshift names a rough temporary stand-in doing duty until the proper thing arrives — and a makeshift table can simply be a crate, grabbed ready-made. Improvised insists something was actually put together on the spot.
